title: U.S. House · Arkansas's 3rd District
area: Northwest Arkansas, including Fayetteville, Fort Smith, Rogers, and Bentonville.

context.text: Both party primaries for this seat were canceled after only one candidate qualified in each: incumbent Steve Womack (R) and Robb Ryerse (D) each advanced unopposed. Bobby Wilson advanced as the Libertarian Party nominee from a February 22, 2026 party convention. Christopher Hocevar filed as an independent but did not make the general-election ballot.

summary.text: Steve Womack is the Republican nominee and incumbent U.S. Representative for Arkansas's 3rd District, seeking re-election. He is a retired Arkansas Army National Guard colonel and former mayor of Rogers.

background.text: Graduated from Arkansas Tech University with a bachelor's degree in 1979.
Served in the Arkansas Army National Guard from 1979 to 2009, retiring with the rank of colonel.
Worked as a radio station manager and consultant; served on the Rogers City Council (1983-1984, 1997-1998) before serving as mayor of Rogers from 1999 to 2010.

record.text: Currently serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, chairing the Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies, and also sitting on the Defense and Financial Services and General Government subcommittees.

summary.text: Robb Ryerse is the Democratic nominee for Arkansas's 3rd Congressional District, running on a platform he describes as "Faith: Powered, Family: Protected, Freedom: Preserved," covering democracy reform, healthcare, and civil rights.

priorities.text: "Faith: Powered" — protect democracy by making voting easier, ending unfair district maps, and getting corporate PAC money out of politics.
"Family: Protected" — raise the minimum wage, protect Social Security, Medicaid and Medicare, and expand affordable housing and paid leave.
"Freedom: Preserved" — expand access to healthcare, protect personal medical decisions, and pass gun laws aimed at school and community safety.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for healthcare access for all without cost being a barrier.
positions.quote: Health Care for All: Everyone should be able to see a doctor without worrying about cost.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for passing gun laws aimed at protecting children at school and families in their communities.
positions.quote: Keep Communities Safe: Pass gun laws that protect kids at school and families in their communities.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for raising the minimum wage.
positions.quote: Better Jobs and Pay: Raise the minimum wage and support local jobs that help families thrive.

positions.summary: Campaign platform says people should be free to make their own decisions about their bodies and lives.
positions.quote: Protect Personal Choices: People should be free to decide about their own bodies and lives.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for investing in clean energy and protecting air, water, and land.
positions.quote: Fight Climate Change: Invest in clean energy and protect our air, water, and land.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for keeping families together and giving immigrants a fair path to citizenship, rather than emphasizing enforcement.
positions.quote: Fair Immigration: Keep families together and give immigrants a fair path to citizenship.

candidates.name: Bobby Wilson
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party's February 22, 2026 state convention.

summary.text: Bobby Wilson is the Libertarian Party nominee for Arkansas's 3rd Congressional District. He previously ran for this seat in 2024, losing to Steve Womack.

background.text: Born in Greenville, North Carolina; has a career background in management.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, detailed biography, or stated policy positions beyond birthplace and profession were found for Wilson.
